title: Explain all @Transactional propagation levels (REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW, SUPPORTS, MANDATORY, NEVER, NESTED) with real-world use cases (especially REQUIRES_NEW for audit logs).
keyPoints: REQUIRED (default): joins the existing transaction or creates a new one if none exists
REQUIRES_NEW: always starts a new independent transaction by suspending the current one
MANDATORY: must run within an existing transaction or throws IllegalTransactionStateException
SUPPORTS: runs in a transaction if one exists, runs non-transactionally otherwise
NOT_SUPPORTED: suspends any existing transaction and runs non-transactionally
NEVER: throws an exception if a transaction already exists
NESTED: creates a savepoint within the existing transaction for partial rollback (JDBC only, not JPA)

s1_definition.oneliner: Propagation controls what happens when one @Transactional method calls another -- REQUIRED joins or creates, REQUIRES_NEW always starts fresh, MANDATORY insists on an existing transaction, and NESTED creates a savepoint.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **REQUIRED (default)** -- joins the caller's transaction if one exists, or creates a new one if none exists. All methods in the call chain share one physical transaction and commit or roll back together.
- **REQUIRES_NEW** -- always creates a new, independent transaction by suspending the caller's transaction. The inner transaction commits or rolls back independently of the outer one.
- **MANDATORY** -- requires an existing transaction. If called without an active transaction, Spring throws `IllegalTransactionStateException`.
- **SUPPORTS** -- runs inside a transaction if one exists, or runs non-transactionally if none exists.
- **NOT_SUPPORTED** -- suspends any existing transaction and runs the method without transactional behavior.
- **NEVER** -- throws an exception if a transaction is currently active. Ensures the method never runs inside a transaction.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, REQUIRED is like a clerk who joins the existing team if one is working on a task, or starts a new team if nobody is working. REQUIRES_NEW is a compliance auditor who always works independently, because the audit record must survive even if the main team's work is undone. MANDATORY is a junior clerk who refuses to work alone and insists on being part of an existing team. NESTED is a clerk who creates a checkpoint within the team's work -- the checkpoint can be undone without undoing everything the team has done so far.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   REQUIRED (default)                     │
│                                                          │
│  Caller has TX?                                          │
│    YES -> join existing TX (same physical TX)             │
│    NO  -> create new TX                                   │
│                                                          │
│  transfer() ──── TX-1 ────────────────────────────────── │
│    └─ ledger.record()  (joins TX-1)                      │
│    └─ All commit or rollback TOGETHER                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   REQUIRES_NEW                            │
│                                                          │
│  Always suspends current TX, creates new TX               │
│                                                          │
│  transfer() ──── TX-1 ─── SUSPENDED ──── TX-1 RESUMED ── │
│    └─ audit.log()  ──── TX-2 ──── COMMIT                 │
│                                                          │
│  TX-2 commits independently of TX-1                      │
│  If TX-1 rolls back, TX-2 survives                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    MANDATORY                              │
│                                                          │
│  Caller has TX?                                          │
│    YES -> join existing TX                                │
│    NO  -> throw IllegalTransactionStateException          │
│                                                          │
│  transfer() ──── TX-1 ────────────────────────────────── │
│    └─ compliance.check()  (joins TX-1 -- OK)             │
│                                                          │
│  compliance.check()  (no TX)                             │
│    └─ EXCEPTION! Must have active TX                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Transaction propagation defines how a @Transactional method behaves when called within an existing transaction. REQUIRED, the default, joins the existing transaction or creates a new one. This is used for the vast majority of business operations because all methods in the call chain commit or roll back together. REQUIRES_NEW always creates a new independent transaction by suspending the outer one, which is essential for audit logs that must persist even when the main transaction rolls back. MANDATORY requires an existing transaction and throws if none exists, which is used for helper methods that must always participate in a caller's transaction.

In Rajesh's loan disbursement service at the National Bank of India, the main disbursement method uses REQUIRED. The compliance check uses MANDATORY to ensure it always runs within the disbursement's transaction. The audit service uses REQUIRES_NEW so that every attempt is recorded for regulatory compliance. When disbursement to a frozen account fails, the main transaction rolls back, but the REQUIRES_NEW audit record is already committed in its own independent transaction. Pankaj, the architect, warns that REQUIRES_NEW holds two database connections simultaneously because the outer transaction's connection is suspended while the inner transaction uses a new one.

The remaining propagation levels cover edge cases. SUPPORTS runs within a transaction if one exists but non-transactionally otherwise. NOT_SUPPORTED suspends any current transaction to avoid holding it during slow operations. NEVER throws if a transaction is present, acting as a safety guard. NESTED creates a savepoint within the existing transaction for partial rollback, though this only works with JDBC and not with JPA.

Remember one sentence: REQUIRED joins or creates (the default for everything), REQUIRES_NEW always creates its own independent transaction (for audit logs), and MANDATORY refuses to work without a caller's transaction.
